narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

A warm day unfolds with a high of 30°C (86°F) and a low of 19°C (66°F). Thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening. Early skies will be mostly cloudy, becoming overcast by midday and staying overcast into the evening. The wind will be north-northeasterly overnight, turning southwest by midday, with peak gusts of 36 km/h (19 kt) ashore and 27 km/h (15 kt) over Winam Gulf. UV reaches a peak index of 9.2. Air quality is forecast at AQI 74. Expect showers and thunderstorms later, with 14.2 mm (0.56 in) of rain likely between 16:00 and 19:00. As of 06:01, reports through 03:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 23°C (73°F); low so far 21°C (70°F); peak sustained 11 km/h (6 kt); sky clear.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS bring temperatures and winds much the same through Monday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Saturday will be mostly cloudy with rain from three of four models, totals between 0.2 and 8.9 mm (0.35 in), highs 27–31°C (81–88°F), and gusts to 28 km/h (15 kt); thunder likely. Sunday remains mostly cloudy, rain from four of four models, 0.5–4.5 mm (0.02–0.18 in), high 30°C (86°F), gusts to 25 km/h (13 kt); thunder likely. Monday continues the pattern, rain from four of four models, 0.7–17.0 mm (0.03–0.67 in), highs 28–30°C (82–86°F), gusts to 24 km/h (13 kt); thunder likely. The record notes the Best Match model holds the best rain record for Day+3.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values signal thunderstorm potential, with Best Match, ECMWF, ICON, and UKMO exceeding the threshold and a peak at 18:00. The model-derived CAPE suggests sudden gusts could surpass the forecast wind, especially if thunderstorms develop. No specific met service warning is issued at this time.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Winam Gulf wind will be east-northeasterly overnight at 6 km/h (3 kt) gusting 10 km/h (5 kt), shifting to south-southwesterly by midday at 6 km/h (3 kt) gusting 15 km/h (8 kt), and increasing to 10 km/h (5 kt) gusting 20 km/h (11 kt) into the evening, with a peak gust of 27 km/h (15 kt). Thunder possible this afternoon raises the risk of stronger gusts.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1006 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1013 hPa) — a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is filling over the next three days. Basin pressure today averages between 1010.7 and 1013.0 hPa, rising by 2.3 hPa over three days. The pressure trend is +0.7 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

Review finds no model clearly superior at Day+0, though GFS misses the thunderstorm and under-forecasts peak wind, while Best Match under-forecasts daytime highs and peak wind. The Best Match model also under-forecasts the high temperature compared with the call. KMD forecasts a max of 29°C (84°F), slightly lower than the call’s 30°C (86°F) high, and aligns on the low of 19°C (66°F). Data sufficiency is strong with 64 checks for Day+0, providing a settled picture despite uneven model coverage.
